newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian avg money rate drops to 8.7 from 19 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian avg money rate drops to 8.7 from 19 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate fell to 8.7 percent on Thursday from 10 percent in shrinking trade.
Turnover dropped to 25.2 from Wednesday's 47.6 million kuna and the most of it -- 18.5 million -- was call money.
But ten million in demand remained unmatched as the banks' liquidity came under pressure ahead of pension payments, due later this week.
The average call money rate eased 20 basis points to 7.8 percent after some lenders accepted lower prices.
Two-week funds were granted at a stable 11 percent and two-month money at 16 percent.
Insurers rolled over seven-day loans at 9.0 and one-month loans at 13 percent, also unchanged.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday weaker at 6.2561 against the dollar and 3.5676 against the German mark. -- Davor Huic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
